document.title: Zookeep Project Ecology Support Burdens
document.purpose: Describe the burdens and support responsibilities that zookeep should carry in order to support a Lion-style project ecology.
author: Lion Kimbro
Wing-Cat (Chat-GPT)

overview.burdens: These burdens are the kinds of support work zookeep should perform when creating, inspecting, or tending a project.
overview.character: Some of these are creation burdens, some are inspection burdens, and some are advisory burdens.
overview.non-comprehensive: This is not comprenehsive, not total.  Take it as suggestive, rather than a complete description.  But these things should all be in the final tool.
overview.goal: The goal is to help projects come into being well and remain coherent over time.

repository-structure-support: Recognize whether a project has a docs/ directory.
Recognize whether a project has a src/ directory in the conventional Python package layout.
Recognize whether a project has a pyproject.toml file when the project is an organized Python package project.
Recognize whether a project has a README.md file.
Recognize whether a project has a .gitignore file.
docs-support: Recognize the raw document convention using numbered filenames such as 0000__name.json.
Inspect whether raw documents appear to follow the expected numbering pattern.
Treat the raw documents as the primary source documents.
Understand that projected documentation areas may exist or may be planned, even if projection is not yet implemented.
Be able to reason about possible future projection rules based on tags, semantic types, semantic base types, or combinations of these.
docs-projection-support: Support the concept that raw documents may be projected into other documentation views or directories.
Be able to describe or validate likely projection destinations such as spec or reference areas.
Understand that projected outputs may be generated artifacts rather than primary authored sources.
Coordinate with .gitignore expectations so generated projected outputs can be ignored while raw documents remain tracked.
python-project-support: Distinguish between a minimal loose Python project and a full organized Python package project.
For organized package projects, expect pyproject.toml and src/package-name/ style layout.
Allow for projects that define scripts or entry points.
Allow for projects that do not define scripts or entry points.
registry-support: Accept a configured location for registry.json.
Understand that registry.json is usually external to the repository.
Treat registry.json as a librarian2 registry file.
Inspect whether the configured registry location exists.
Inspect whether the registry file is readable and structurally valid enough to use.
Inspect whether the registry contains entries for core external resources needed by the project ecology.
external-resource-support: Check whether JSON standards documents are present in the registry.
Check whether those documents are identifiable by stable identifier.
Check whether the personal dictionary is present in the registry.
Respect the rule that the personal dictionary should not be automatically loaded by default.
inspection-support: Inspect both repository-local structure and ecology-external references.
Report missing expected files or directories.
Report uncertainty clearly when a feature is aspirational, planned, or only partially implemented.
advisory-support: Explain what appears healthy or coherent in the repository ecology.
Explain what appears absent or weak.
Describe likely next steps without pretending that unimplemented systems already exist.
Respect variation across different breeds of project directory.

docs-checklist: raw documents follow numbered naming convention
raw documents are treated as source documents
registry-checklist: registry contains core referenced documents by identifier
external-resource-checklist: JSON standards documents are discoverable through registry
personal dictionary is discoverable through registry
personal dictionary is not auto-loaded by default

important-restraints.do-not-pretend: zookeep should not pretend that the docs projection system already exists in finished form.
important-restraints.do-not-over-assume: zookeep should not assume that all Python projects are fully packaged projects.
important-restraints.do-not-auto-load-dictionary: zookeep should not automatically load the personal dictionary by default.
important-restraints.respect-variation: zookeep should support recognizable form without forcing every project into exactly one shape.
